name: TGV SRAAC Ltd
tagline: Forward-integrated, low-cost chlor-alkali producer trading below book value on a genuine solar-driven cost reduction, but Q4 FY26 already shows the caustic tailwind cooling just as Reliance/Adani's confirmed large new capacity looms for 2027-28
business_overview: TGV SRAAC (formerly Sree Rayalseema Alkalies & Allied Chemicals) produces chlor-alkali products (caustic soda, chlorine), chloromethanes, castor derivatives and fatty acids, with a strategy of forward-integrating chlorine into higher-value downstream chemicals and aggressively adding captive solar power to cut input costs.
fundamentals_narrative: Cheap on an absolute basis (7.9x trailing P/E, 0.85x book) with double-digit ROCE and continuing growth: FY26 full year sales +13.2% to Rs 1,749 Cr, net profit +53.3% to Rs 92 Cr; Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) sales Rs 543 Cr (+10.3% YoY), PAT ~Rs 45 Cr (+17.2% YoY, EPS Rs 4.24). But Q4 FY26 already showed the first signs of the margin cycle turning: OPM contracted 72bps QoQ to 16.56% (gross margin 17.81%->15.72%) on rising employee costs (+10.26% QoQ) and interest expense (+76% QoQ) — a caution flag given the 3-year average ROE is only 7.26% and 3-year profit CAGR is -29% (FY24 cycle trough: sales -34%, OPM cratered to 3.8%).
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 165 fetched posts (2024-11 to 2026-08), single batch. Sentiment is consistently constructive on the operating story: heavy forward integration into chlorine derivatives insulates the company from industry-wide negative chlorine realizations (a headwind DCM Shriram and others explicitly flagged in their own concalls), aggressive captive-solar capacity additions are structurally lowering power costs (the largest input cost in caustic production), and China anti-involution measures plus European capacity shutdowns (Ineos Inovyn, Dow) are seen as multi-year caustic-price tailwinds. The recurring negative theme across the whole period is management's poor shareholder communication — no press releases, minimal concalls, low dividends despite strong profitability, and a pattern of pre-emptive write-offs from ongoing APERC (state electricity regulator) power-cost litigation.
community_signal: Phaeton was the most technically detailed and consistently engaged poster across the thread (not on the trusted roster but highly substantive), tracking ECU (caustic+chlorine) realizations, capacity additions, and APERC litigation write-offs in granular detail. Trusted user Prabhat_Mohanty repeatedly argued the stock is 'damn cheap from whatever angle' given replacement-cost economics, capacity build-up, and improving low-cost power position, but explicitly attributed the persistent undervaluation to 'promoters' total disdain for retail investors' rather than any operational weakness.

trusted_signals.note: Argued the stock is significantly undervalued on replacement-cost and capacity-build-up grounds, attributing the languishing valuation specifically to poor promoter/shareholder communication (no concalls, minimal disclosure) rather than to weak fundamentals, which he called genuinely strong.

Reiterated conviction that the stock is cheap 'from whatever angle' (management capability, capacity, integrity, financial ratios) but flagged that better shareholder communication (concalls, dividends) would be needed for the market to properly re-rate it.

bse_notes: History of litigation with Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC) over retrospective power-cost demands, which the company contests and occasionally has to pre-emptively write off, then write back when it wins — a recurring, disclosed pattern rather than a new red flag. Six-product-line capacity expansion (KOH +27,150 TPA, Liquid Chlorine +17,160 TPA, Methylene Chloride +17,817 TPA, and others) announced effective April 2026. Solar capacity added in steady 2.5 MWp increments through 2026, reaching 62.90 MWp (from 55.40 MWp in March 2026).
bull_case: Cheap valuation (7.9x trailing P/E, 0.85x book value) alongside double-digit ROCE (13%) and continuing double-digit growth (FY26 sales +13.2%, PAT +53.3%; Q1 FY27 sales +10.3%/PAT +17.2% YoY)

Structural cost advantage building via aggressive captive-solar capacity additions (55.4 MWp to 62.9 MWp through 2026 alone), directly reducing the largest input cost (power) in caustic production — verified as actually executing on schedule via repeated 2026 BSE filings, not just a stated plan

Forward integration into chloromethanes/derivatives (six-product-line capacity expansion effective April 2026) insulates against industry-wide negative chlorine realizations that are hurting less-integrated peers (DCM Shriram, Gujarat Alkalies)

China anti-involution capacity cuts and European shutdowns (Ineos Inovyn, Dow) are genuine, multi-year, industry-wide caustic-price tailwinds independent of company execution — corroborated this pass by actual Indian caustic soda price data rising ~19% (Apr-Jul 2026) on demand-led recovery
Consistent promoter buying at multiple price points (Rs 97-111/share) through 2025-26; promoter holding rising slowly (63.18% in 2023 to 64.27% Jun 2026) with zero pledge
bear_case: Large new caustic capacity from Reliance and Adani (Adani's 2,200 TPD Mundra project alone is described as India's largest chlor-alkali project, targeted live by 2027-28) is a real, sizeable, and now well-corroborated medium-term oversupply risk the community itself actively debates

Q4 FY26 already showed the margin cycle turning before any of that new competing capacity has even landed: OPM contracted 72bps QoQ to 16.56%, gross margin compressed 17.81%->15.72%, on rising employee costs (+10.26% QoQ) and a 76% QoQ jump in interest expense — a live warning that the current 16-18% OPM band may be nearer a cycle peak than a new normal

Persistently poor shareholder communication — no press releases after results, minimal concalls, low dividend payout (12.5% of profits over 3 years) despite strong profitability — a real governance/communication gap even without a disqualifying red flag
Recurring APERC power-cost litigation creates noisy, hard-to-model quarterly write-off/write-back swings in reported profit

Caustic soda is fundamentally a cyclical commodity chemical — 3-year average ROE of just 7.26% and a 3-year profit CAGR of -29% (FY24 trough: sales -34%, OPM 3.8%) underline how quickly the current tailwind (China cuts, Europe shutdowns) could reverse as new domestic capacity comes online
verdict_headline: Genuinely cheap, low-cost chlor-alkali operator with real, executing cost-reduction and forward-integration programs, but this remains a cyclical commodity-chemical business whose margin cycle already shows early signs of turning just as large new domestic capacity is confirmed for 2027-28
verdict_reasoning: Strong recent execution (double-digit growth, cheap valuation below book, real and verified solar-driven cost reduction and capacity expansion) makes this a credible value/GARP idea, but caustic soda remains a cyclical commodity where large new domestic capacity (Reliance, and Adani's confirmed India's-largest 2,200 TPD Mundra project) is a real 2027-28 supply risk that caps the multi-year compounding case

This pass downgrades the moat read from 'yes' to 'weak': captive solar and forward integration lower TGV's own cost base but don't create pricing power or switching costs, and better-capitalized new entrants (Reliance, Adani) will likely build even more efficient plants — cost reduction here is a margin cushion, not a durable moat

The persistent shareholder-communication gap, while not a disqualifying red flag, is exactly the kind of governance friction that has kept this cheap for years and could continue to do so regardless of operational performance
Sits as 'neither' primarily on business-model grounds (cyclical commodity chemical, four_box score 2.5) rather than execution — a reasonable value holding, not a multibagger thesis

four_box.note: China anti-involution capacity cuts + European shutdowns (Ineos Inovyn, Dow) remain a real multi-year industry tailwind, corroborated this pass by actual Indian caustic price data (+19% Apr-Jul 2026); but large new caustic capacity from Reliance/Adani (Adani's 2,200 TPD Mundra project confirmed as India's largest chlor-alkali project, targeted live 2027-28) is a real, confirmed oversupply risk - tam no. Downgraded moat from yes to weak this pass: captive-solar/forward-integration cost reduction is real and executing on schedule but is a cost cushion, not pricing power or switching costs, and new entrants will likely be built even more efficiently. ~7.9x trailing P/E, 0.85x book - valuation yes. Score 2.5 (2.0-2.5 band); kept as neither on business-model grounds (cyclical commodity, no durable moat) rather than invoking the valuation exception.

track_record.note: Screener FY18-FY26: rev growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% both cleared in only 3 of 9 (FY19 15%/22%, FY22 51%/21%, FY23 53%/38%) - the caustic up-cycle years. FY24 collapsed (-34% sales, 5% ROCE); FY25-26 recovered on revenue but ROCE stuck at 10-13%. Cyclical commodity chemical.

quality_metrics.note: ROCE 5%->10%->13% FY24-26 off a cyclical trough; OPM 9%->13%->18% (FY24-26 full-year) as solar cuts power cost, but Q4FY26 already shows a 72bp QoQ sequential OPM decline to 16.56% - the expansion may be topping out. Borrowings ~Rs357cr FY26 vs EBITDA ~Rs315-330cr (~1.1x). Trailing-3y FCF ~breakeven (CFO Rs697cr vs capex Rs705cr FY24-26) - heavy captive-solar + forward-integration capex; returns improving but 3-yr avg ROE still just 7.26% and dividend payout only 12.5% of profits, so capex/shareholder-return efficiency reads neutral, not positive.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: at ~7.9x trailing P/E (0.85x book) the market prices mid-cycle normalisation / a flattening earnings path; roughly 0-5% EPS CAGR justifies today's multiple on an ~8-10x cyclical exit
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: revenue +8-12%, OPM likely plateauing in the mid-to-high-teens as solar cost savings partly offset the Q4FY26 cost-inflation signal, PAT growth decelerating from FY26's +53% toward the mid-teens
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: flat-to-down risk as Reliance/Adani caustic capacity (notably Adani's confirmed 2,200 TPD Mundra project) lands 2027-28
market_expectation.gap_basis: cheap on trailing earnings and book value with a real, executing solar-driven cost program; but Q4FY26's early margin deceleration plus the now well-corroborated 2027-28 domestic caustic oversupply (Reliance, Adani) and weak shareholder communication cap the re-rating - the market's caution looks roughly fair, not clearly wrong.
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

key_new_facts: Adani's Mundra chlor-alkali project (2,200 TPD) is confirmed by industry press as India's largest chlor-alkali project under construction, materially firming up the 2027-28 oversupply risk that was previously community speculation
Q4 FY26 already shows the caustic margin cycle beginning to turn (72bp sequential OPM compression, rising employee and interest costs) - a live signal that predates the new competing capacity

Trading at 0.85x book value (P/B) alongside 7.9x trailing P/E - genuinely cheap on both metrics

open_questions: Whether the Q4FY26 margin compression is a one-off (cost timing) or the start of a genuine cyclical turn
Exact commissioning date for Adani's Mundra project and how much of its capacity is caustic vs other chlor-alkali derivatives

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Low-Medium. Fresh filings confirm the business is executing well operationally (solar build-out, forward integration, continued double-digit growth, trades below book), but this pass firms up two cautions that were softer before: the Reliance/Adani 2027-28 oversupply risk is now confirmed via credible industry press rather than just community debate, and Q4FY26 already shows the margin cycle beginning to turn before that new capacity has even landed. The moat read is downgraded from yes to weak (cost cushion, not pricing power), taking four_box score from 3.0 to 2.5. Remains a genuine value/GARP holding, not a 10x thesis.
